title: Error propagation through the date/text value family: 7 of 7 vs Excel
status_plain: DATEVALUE and TIMEVALUE (with their in-file siblings DAYS360 and DATEDIF) collapsed any error argument to #VALUE!, and ARRAYTOTEXT stringified it to the text "#N/A". After the fix all five propagate the incoming error unchanged with its code preserved, while errors inside an array argument stay textified. The source scores this "7/7 vs Excel" - a group total over seven probe cases across the five surfaces, not a per-surface figure. The 7/7 sentence does not restate a build; the build for the resweep it sits inside is live Excel 16.0 build 20026, stated in the section header and the Ref notes.

counts.quoted_source_sentence:
- **Error-propagation sub-finding — fixed (2026-06-20).** `DATEVALUE`/`TIMEVALUE` (and their
  in-file siblings `DAYS360`/`DATEDIF`) collapsed any error argument to `#VALUE!` via
  `coerce_*.map_err(|_| Coercion)`; `ARRAYTOTEXT` stringified it to the text "#N/A". All now
  propagate the incoming error unchanged with its code preserved (`first_error_arg` /
  scalar-error guard), while errors *inside* an array argument stay textified
  (`ARRAYTOTEXT({1;#N/A})` → "1, #N/A"). 7/7 vs Excel; regression test
  `date_value_family::tests::error_args_propagate_unchanged_through_value_family`.

reader_warning: This is an error-placement measurement on the structural axis. It says nothing about any of these five surfaces' numeric results.
